name: Three-Thirteen Rummy
description: Rummy variant with eleven rounds. In round 1 three cards are dealt to each player, in round 2 four cards, and so on up to thirteen in round 11. Each round has a different wild card: round 1 threes are wild, round 2 fours, up to kings wild in round 11. Players draw one card from the stock or top of the discard pile, then discard one. Object is to form all cards into sets of three or more of the same rank or runs of three or more in the same suit; aces rank low. Lowest total penalty after eleven rounds wins.

history.origins: Three-Thirteen Rummy variant from the USA where card count per hand increases from 3 to 13 across successive rounds.
timeline: 20th century: Rummy variant from the United States with round-based hand sizes and wild cards; documented in card-game literature.

setup.dealing: Eleven rounds. First dealer is chosen at random; the turn to deal passes to the left after each round. In round 1 three cards are dealt to each player, in round 2 four cards, and so on until round 11 when thirteen cards each are dealt. The remainder is placed face down as the stock; the top card is turned face up beside it to start the discard pile. One deck for two players, two decks for three or four.

rules.objective: Form all cards in hand into valid combinations: sets of three or more cards of the same rank, or runs of three or more cards in the same suit in sequence. Aces rank low. Unmatched cards at round end count as penalty points; the player with the lowest total score after eleven rounds wins.
rules.gameplay: The player to dealer's left begins; play is clockwise. Each turn consists of drawing one card (from the top of the stock or the top card of the discard pile; only the top of the discard may be taken) and then discarding one card face up onto the discard pile. A player may go out when, after drawing, they can arrange all but one card into sets and runs, discard that card, and announce they are out; each other player gets one more turn, then the round ends when the turn returns to the player who went out.
keyRules: Eleven rounds with 3 to 13 cards dealt per round; dealer rotates left.
Wild card equals the number of cards dealt that round (round 1 threes wild, round 11 kings wild).
Valid combinations: sets of three or more same rank; runs of three or more same suit in sequence; aces low.
Draw one from stock or top of discard, then discard one. No laying off on other players' melds.

strategy.basic: Minimize deadwood by forming sets and runs; use wild cards in combinations where they replace missing cards.
strategy.intermediate: Track which cards have been discarded to infer what opponents need; take from the discard only when it completes or extends a combination.
strategy.advanced: Plan round-by-round: in early rounds with few cards, prioritize flexibility; in later rounds with more cards, optimize for going out before opponents.
tips: Wild cards can form a set by themselves or fill gaps in runs.
Aces are low only; Q-K-A is not a valid run.

variations.name: Ace high or low
variations.description: Aces may be used high or low so A-K-Q is a valid run; an ace left in hand at round end costs 15 points instead of 1.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes scoring and meld evaluation but no engine override fields have been wired yet.

variations.name: Face card scoring
variations.description: Some groups score 10 points for Jacks, Queens, and Kings instead of 11, 12, and 13 as in the base rules.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Face-card point tweaks are handled in scoring logic and have not been modeled as structured engine overrides.

variations.name: Jokers as wilds
variations.description: Jokers are added as extra wild cards; a joker left in hand at round end scores 20 penalty points.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Use of jokers as wild cards is described in rules text but not yet wired into engine override fields.

variations.name: 3-13 Speed
variations.description: Simultaneous drawing and discarding controlled by a caller; for large groups.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Speed variant affects timing and UX only; no separate structured engine overrides are defined yet.

variations.name: Five Crowns
variations.description: Proprietary version using a five-suited pack.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Five Crowns is treated as a related proprietary game, not a direct ruleset override for this engine.

variations.name: Deuces Aren't Wild
variations.description: Variant with an additional 14-card round and a bonus round in the event of a tie.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Round-count and bonus-round tweaks are documented narratively and not yet captured as engine overrides.

scoring.description: At round end each player arranges their hand into sets and runs. Unmatched cards score penalty: Ace 1, 2–10 face value, Jack 11, Queen 12, King 13. Totals accumulate across rounds; lowest total after round 11 wins.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest total penalty score after eleven rounds wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Rummy with eleven rounds (3 to 13 cards per round) and round-based wild cards; lowest penalty total wins.
